title: Toxic Opens to Rs 140 Crore Worldwide, But Day 2 Drop Raises Questions for Yash
excerpt: Yash's post-KGF gamble delivered a massive Rs 101 crore net on day one in India, yet a steep 64% second-day decline puts pressure on the weekend to determine Toxic's commercial fate.
body:
• Toxic collected Rs 101.10 crore net (Rs 120.75 crore gross) in India on day one, with a worldwide gross of approximately Rs 140.75 crore — the second-biggest opening of 2026 behind Dhurandhar 2.
  • Day 2 saw a sharp 64% decline to Rs 36.40 crore net in India, bringing the two-day domestic gross to Rs 164.50 crore and worldwide total to Rs 190.75 crore.
  • Hindi markets contributed Rs 55 crore net on day one, outperforming the Kannada version's Rs 25 crore, marking a shift in Yash's audience geography.
  • The film's steep second-day fall contrasts with KGF: Chapter 2's 22% day-two dip, making the weekend hold critical for long-term profitability.

Yash's highly anticipated return to the big screen with Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups has delivered one of the biggest opening days in Indian cinema this year — and one of the sharpest second-day corrections.

The Geetu Mohandas-directed gangster drama collected Rs 101.10 crore net in India on its August 26 opening day, translating to a gross of Rs 120.75 crore domestically and approximately Rs 140.75 crore worldwide, according to tracking platform Sacnilk. The figures place Toxic as the second-biggest opener of 2026, narrowly behind Dhurandhar 2's Rs 145.55 crore debut.

A Pan-India Opening, Led by Hindi

The territorial breakdown reveals a notable shift in Yash's commercial footprint. The Hindi version emerged as the largest contributor with Rs 55 crore in net collections — more than double the Kannada version's sub-Rs 25 crore figure despite strong occupancy in Karnataka. The Telugu release added Rs 16 crore, while the overseas market contributed Rs 20 crore.

The numbers underscore Yash's evolution from a regional star into a pan-India draw following KGF: Chapter 2. Toxic's Hindi performance exceeds opening-day Hindi collections of several major Bollywood releases, while its worldwide debut surpassed the day-one grosses of Pathaan (Rs 106 crore), Animal (Rs 116 crore), and Jawan (Rs 129 crore).

Day 2 Tells a Different Story

The momentum, however, did not hold. Toxic recorded Rs 36.40 crore net on its second day across 22,629 shows, a 64% decline from day one. The India gross fell to Rs 43.75 crore on Thursday, taking the two-day domestic gross to Rs 164.50 crore and worldwide total to Rs 190.75 crore.

Toxic's day-two decline of 64% stands in stark contrast to KGF: Chapter 2, which dropped just 22% on its second day and reached Rs 206.50 crore net in two days.

Karnataka, still the film's strongest market, contributed Rs 10.75 crore on day two after a Rs 30.50 crore opening — a 65% drop. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana fell sharply from Rs 18.50 crore to Rs 4.25 crore. Tamil Nadu's collections slid from Rs 6.75 crore to Rs 1.75 crore, with competition from new Tamil releases Hi and Once More expected to squeeze screen counts further from Friday.

What This Means for Yash and Kannada Cinema

Toxic arrived carrying an A certificate and largely unfavourable critical reactions, factors that industry analysts say explain the front-loaded opening followed by a steep correction. The film registered 1.5 million ticket sales across BookMyShow and District before premiere shows concluded, and major theatre chains in Mumbai introduced 6 AM and midnight screenings to manage demand — a testament to Yash's star power regardless of critical reception.

For Kannada cinema, the opening is symbolically significant. Toxic's Rs 140 crore worldwide debut is the biggest day-one number for a Kannada-origin film, even accounting for its multilingual release strategy. The film was shot simultaneously in Kannada and English and released in five languages — a distribution model that may become a template for future Kannada tentpole releases.

The commercial question now is whether Toxic can stabilize through the weekend. With an estimated production and marketing budget that industry reports peg as one of the costliest for a Kannada film, the difference between a weekday stabilization and a continued slide will determine whether Toxic joins the profitable blockbuster tier or becomes a cautionary tale about opening-day euphoria.
